title: Mara and the Oath
premise: Vesper Crane, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that fell silent generations ago, has survived by hiding in the valley where magic cannot follow. When the crown's witch-hunt reaches the valley and their sworn brothers turn them in, Vesper flees with Mara, a fire-gifted child who may be the last vessel of dragon-fire. Together with a disgraced cartographer and an exiled priest, they search for the door out of a country that was erased from every map. In the end, Vesper must choose between renewing the silent god's oath or breaking it to carry the last flame through the door—choosing found family over inherited duty.
about_author: Oscar Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border treaties of defunct nations before turning to fiction. They write about oaths, maps, and the people who fall through both.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet the mercenary company in the magic-dead valley, where Vesper maintains the shrine to the silent god and hides their own dormant gift. A crown herald arrives announcing the hunt for the gifted. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the illusion of safety cracking.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A burned child, Mara, stumbles into camp carrying living dragon-fire in her palms; the company votes to surrender her for the bounty. Vesper's gift flickers awake near her for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the first pull of loyalty beyond the oath.

chapters.title: Brothers at the Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The company captain gives Vesper until dawn to hand Mara over. Instead Vesper cuts their oath-cord and flees with the girl through the valley's edge, where magic resumes like a tide. Emotional beat: betrayal and liberation entwined.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hiding in a river town, they meet Ilsa Vane, a disgraced royal cartographer imprisoned for mapping a country that no longer exists—and who claims its last door still stands. Emotional beat: wary hope; Mara begins trusting strangers.

chapters.title: What the Crown Burns
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The party witnesses a public pyre of accused gift-bearers and learns the hunt's true purpose: the crown is harvesting magic to reignite a dead relic. Emotional beat: horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Exile's Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They shelter with Brother Anselm, an exiled priest of the silent god, who reveals the god did not abandon the world—it was devoured, and its last spark sleeps inside Vesper's broken oath. Emotional beat: grief reframed; inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Crossing the Unmapped Reach
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pursued by witch-hunters, the group crosses the erased country using Ilsa's forbidden maps, losing supplies and nearly losing Anselm. Mara's fire flares to save him, marking them from the sky. Emotional beat: found family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Price of the Flame
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cornered at the border ruins, Vesper bargains with the crown's inquisitor—revealing themselves fully—to buy the others time. Ilsa is captured; the map half-burned. Emotional beat: sacrifice and guilt; the old oath's ghost whispers renewal.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the door of the vanished country, Vesper must feed the silent god's sleeping spark—or let it die and open the door with Mara's dragon-fire instead. Vesper breaks the oath forever, choosing Mara. Emotional beat: climax; inheritance transformed into choice.

chapters.title: A Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Through the door lies the erased land, alive and waiting; Ilsa is ransomed free, Anselm plants a new shrine without a god, and Mara's flame settles into hearth-light rather than weapon-fire. Emotional beat: belonging—not inherited, but built.
